title: Defend: CBC alignment check before pool acquire prevents word32 underflow in IV update
description: crypto2dev_cipher rejects CBC with data_sz not aligned to AES_BLOCK_SIZE (line 692) before pool acquisition. A reviewer might suggest removing this as 'redundant' since wolfSSL's wc_AesCbcEncrypt validates alignment. The check protects against a word32 underflow: the IV update at line 831 computes 'src + data_sz - AES_BLOCK_SIZE'. If data_sz < AES_BLOCK_SIZE (e.g., 0 or 7), the subtraction underflows word32 and the XMEMCPY reads from an arbitrary address. wolfSSL only enforces alignment when WOLFSSL_AES_CBC_LENGTH_CHECKS is defined, which is not the default. Without the check, an application calling the CryptoCb API directly with unaligned data would cause a memory read at an arbitrary address with no error. The BAD_FUNC_ARG early return is not redundant; it is the only defense against underflow on non-default builds.
